- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- backstage-scaffold: Scaffold a new integration system using a Backstage blueprint template (golden-record, distribution, or point-to-point)
- code-assist: This sop guides the implementation of code tasks using test-driven development principles, following a structured Explore, Plan, Code, Commit workflow. It balances automation with user collaboration while adhering to existing package patterns and prioritizing readability and extensibility. The agent acts as a Technical Implementation Partner and TDD Coach - providing guidance, generating test cases and implementation code that follows existing patterns, avoids over-engineering, and produces idiomatic, modern code in the target language.
- code-task-generator: This SOP generates structured code task files from rough descriptions, ideas, PDD implementation plans, or Intropy shaping packages. It automatically detects the input type and creates properly formatted code task files following the code task format specification. For PDD plans, it processes implementation steps one at a time to allow for learning and adaptation between steps. For shaping packages, it generates an implementation plan from the shaped design and then produces tasks from the approved plan. When the work involves scaffolding a new project, it emits a dedicated scaffold task that uses the `intropy` CLI to generate the project skeleton before any implementation begins.
- codebase-summary: This sop analyzes a codebase and generates comprehensive documentation including structured metadata files that describe the system architecture, components, interfaces, and workflows. It can create targeted documentation files like AGENTS.md (README for AI agents), README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, or generate a complete documentation ecosystem. The documentation is organized to make it easy for AI assistants to understand the system and help with development tasks.
- dotnet-tdd-expert: Analyze .NET libraries and their xUnit test suites to suggest improvements to test quality, structure, and TDD practices. Use this skill whenever the user mentions .NET tests, xUnit, test quality, test review, test improvements, test coverage analysis, TDD in C#, or asks to review or improve unit tests in a .NET codebase — even if they don't explicitly say "TDD" or "test-driven development". Also trigger when the user shares C# test files and wants feedback, or when they ask about testing patterns, mocking strategies, or test naming conventions in .NET.
- eval: EvalKit is a conversational evaluation framework for AI agents that guides you through creating robust evaluations using the Strands Evals SDK. Through natural conversation, you can plan evaluations, generate test data, execute evaluations, and analyze results.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- golang-cli: Golang CLI application development. Use when building, modifying, or reviewing a Go CLI tool — especially for command structure, flag handling, configuration layering, version embedding, exit codes, I/O patterns, signal handling, shell completion, argument validation, and CLI unit testing. Also triggers when code uses cobra, viper, or urfave/cli.
- golang-performance: Golang performance optimization patterns and methodology - if X bottleneck, then apply Y. Covers allocation reduction, CPU efficiency, memory layout, GC tuning, pooling, caching, and hot-path optimization. Use when profiling or benchmarks have identified a bottleneck and you need the right optimization pattern to fix it. Also use when performing performance code review to suggest improvements or benchmarks that could help identify quick performance gains. Not for measurement methodology (see golang-benchmark skill) or debugging workflow (see golang-troubleshooting skill).
- golden-path-docs: Generate complete Golden Path tutorial scaffolds for Backstage TechDocs. Produces mkdocs.yml configuration and multi-part markdown tutorial structures following Spotify-inspired golden path patterns, tailored to Intropy's integration domain model (Blueprints, Blocks, Connectors, Systems). Use this skill whenever someone asks to create golden path documentation, scaffold a TechDocs tutorial, write onboarding docs for a new integration pattern, document a Blueprint or Block, or set up step-by-step developer guides for Backstage. Also trigger when the user mentions "golden path", "TechDocs", "integration tutorial", "onboarding docs", "developer guide for Backstage", or wants to document how to build something using Intropy's opinionated tooling.
- integrio-diagrams: Compose Intropy/Integrio technical diagrams — pipelines, distributed traces, error-routing, topology cards, layered architecture — as plain inline SVG built from a shared brand primitive vocabulary (node dots, concentric rings, 3×3 dot grids, curved connectors, stage chips, panels, dapr-style labelled dashed containers, filled hexagons for integration units, timeline bars). Use this skill ANY time a labeled technical diagram is added or edited on the Intropy site (funktioner.html, arkitektur.html, index.html) or when an existing diagram feels generic/"AI-generated" and needs to be rebuilt on-brand. Trigger even if the user just says "the diagram", "the figure", "FIG F4.1", "the pipeline graphic", "the trace visual", "the architecture SVG", or "make this diagram look less generic". For decorative art (heroes, dividers, OG cards, spot illustrations) use integrio-imagery instead — this skill is for diagrams that carry labeled meaning.
- intropy-docs: Write, update, or review any Intropy documentation for Backstage TechDocs — reference pages, pattern catalog entries, architecture overviews, onboarding content, and environment setup guides. Use for any task involving Intropy concepts: blocks (Extractor, Loader, Reconciler, Assembler), blueprints (Golden Record, Product Sync, Order Import), archetypes (Pub/Sub, Aggregator, API Service), connectors, or the Intropy model. Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions documentation, reference docs, pattern catalog, TechDocs, architecture docs, developer guide, or wants to explain or write up any Intropy concept — even if they don't explicitly say "documentation".
- next-best-practices: Next.js best practices - file conventions, RSC boundaries, data patterns, async APIs, metadata, error handling, route handlers, image/font optimization, bundling
- pdd: This sop guides you through the process of transforming a rough idea into a detailed design document with an implementation plan and todo list. It follows the Prompt-Driven Development methodology to systematically refine your idea, conduct necessary research, create a comprehensive design, and develop an actionable implementation plan. The process is designed to be iterative, allowing movement between requirements clarification and research as needed.
- pipeline-runs: Query pipeline execution runs for a given integration tag. Looks up services in the Backstage catalog by tag, then queries Tempo for matching pipeline traces. Use this skill when someone asks to "show runs", "list executions", "find pipeline traces", or "check pipeline activity" for an integration identifier like "int201", "int305", etc. Also trigger when the user mentions "runs for <tag>", "pipeline runs", "trace search for integration", or wants to see what happened for a specific integration over a time range.
- re-shape: This SOP performs targeted reshaping after a failed gate or major implementation delta.  It updates the shaping package with versioned changes rather than restarting from scratch.
- service-setup: Scaffold a new platform infrastructure service into the GitOps repository with the correct kustomize base/overlay structure, Helm chart integration, HA configuration, and full documentation (architecture page, operations page, disaster recovery section, ADR entries, and mkdocs.yml updates). Use this skill whenever someone asks to add a new infrastructure component, deploy a new Helm chart to the service plane, set up a new platform service, onboard a new operator or tool to the cluster, or scaffold GitOps manifests for a service. Also trigger when the user mentions "add service to gitops", "new helm chart setup", "deploy X to the cluster", "add infrastructure component", or wants to create kustomize manifests for a new tool.
- shape-review: This SOP runs after implementation starts (or after plan generation) to validate whether shaping decisions were complete, correct, and actionable.  It closes the loop by turning implementation feedback into either: - `accepted` (shaping holds) - `conditional` (minor clarifications needed) - `reopen` (major reshaping required)
- shaping: This SOP converts a business integration request into a shaped design package ready for implementation. It ensures every engagement maps to Intropy's golden paths, resolves key decisions through clarification and validation, and produces traceable artifacts that preserve design rationale alongside code.  Shaping is complete when a coding SOP can consume the output without requiring further architectural decisions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- chrome-devtools-mcp:a11y-debugging: Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for accessibility (a11y) debugging and auditing based on web.dev guidelines. Use when testing semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus states, keyboard navigation, tap targets, and color contrast.
- chrome-devtools-mcp:chrome-devtools: Uses Chrome DevTools via MCP for efficient debugging, troubleshooting and browser automation. Use when debugging web pages, automating browser interactions, analyzing performance, or inspecting network requests. This skill does not apply to `--slim` mode (MCP configuration).
- chrome-devtools-mcp:chrome-devtools-cli: Use this skill to write shell scripts or run shell commands to automate tasks in the browser or otherwise use Chrome DevTools via CLI.
- chrome-devtools-mcp:debug-optimize-lcp: Guides debugging and optimizing Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) using Chrome DevTools MCP tools. Use this skill whenever the user asks about LCP performance, slow page loads, Core Web Vitals optimization, or wants to understand why their page's main content takes too long to appear. Also use when the user mentions "largest contentful paint", "page load speed", "CWV", or wants to improve how fast their hero image or main content renders.
- chrome-devtools-mcp:memory-leak-debugging: Diagnoses and resolves memory leaks in JavaScript/Node.js applications. Use when a user reports high memory usage, OOM errors, or wants to analyze heapsnapshots or run memory leak detection tools like memlab.
- chrome-devtools-mcp:troubleshooting: Uses Chrome DevTools MCP and documentation to troubleshoot connection and target issues. Trigger this skill when list_pages, new_page, or navigate_page fail, or when the server initialization fails.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---
name: backstage-scaffold
description: >-
  Scaffold a new integration system by calling the Backstage scaffolder API
  with a blueprint template (golden-record, distribution, or point-to-point).
  Trigger when asked to scaffold, create, or bootstrap an integration system
  through Backstage. Trigger phrases: "scaffold an integration system",
  "create a golden-record integration", "new distribution integration".
  SKIP if scaffolding locally with the intropy CLI — that goes to
  `intropy-getting-started`.
---

# Backstage Blueprint Scaffolding

Scaffold a complete integration system by calling the Backstage scaffolder API.

## Available Blueprints

| Template name | Description |
|---|---|
| `golden-record-blueprint` | Extractors, reconciler, and loaders for a single source of truth |
| `distribution-blueprint` | Single source to multiple destinations |
| `point-to-point-blueprint` | Simple source-to-destination integration |

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the blueprint

Ask the user which blueprint to use if not already clear from context. If the user says something like "golden record", "distribution", or "point-to-point", map it to the corresponding template name above.

### 2. Fetch template parameters

Use the Backstage MCP `fetch-template-metadata` tool with the exact `name` from the table above to get the template's required parameters and steps. Do NOT fetch all templates — always filter by name.

### 3. Gather parameter values

Look up available options from the Backstage catalog to help the user:
- **Groups** (for `owner`): use `fetch-catalog-entities` with `kind: Group`
- **Domains** (for `domain`): use `fetch-catalog-entities` with `kind: Domain`

apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: hello-world
  title: Hello World
  description: Minimal example scaffolder template for the Intropy integration platform.
  tags:
    - hello-world
    - example
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: example
spec:
  owner: group:default/platform
  type: example

  parameters:
    - title: Greeting
      required:
        - name
      properties:
        name:
          title: Name
          type: string
          description: Person or system to greet.

  steps:
    # ---- Generate skeleton ----
    - id: fetch-skeleton
      name: Fetch hello-world skeleton
      action: fetch:plain
      input:
        url: ../skeletons/nunjucks/hello-world
        targetPath: ./_cache

    - id: render-hello
      name: Render hello-world
      action: intropy:workspace:template
      input:
        sourcePath: ./_cache
        targetPath: ./output
        values:
          name: ${{ parameters.name }}

    # ---- Cleanup ----
    - id: cleanup-cache
      name: Clean up cache
      action: fs:delete
      input:
        files:
          - ./_cache

# Implementation Plan: `intropy:int:create` Scaffolder Action + PoC Template

## Overview

Add a custom scaffolder action to the existing `scaffolder/intropy-actions` backend module that shells out to the `intropy` Go CLI (`int create`), get the static binary into the backend image via a multi-stage `COPY --from`, and ship one PoC template (hello-world blueprint) that generates code and opens a GitLab MR following the golden-record template's conventions.

Verified facts this plan relies on:
- `executeShellCommand` IS exported from the installed `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node@0.13.2`, but its implementation (checked `node_modules/@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node/dist/actions/executeShellCommand.cjs.js`) rejects with only `Command ${command} failed, exit code: ${code}` — no structured exit code, no stderr capture. Since we need exit-2-vs-1 mapping and a stderr tail in the error message, we write a ~40-line spawn wrapper modeled on it instead.
- `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node-test-utils` is NOT installed (checked node_modules) — the existing test file hand-tests helpers without an action harness. We add the test-utils package as a devDependency.
- Backstage 1.50.4; module registration at `packages/backend/src/index.ts:43`; helm chart at `charts/intropy-backstage` with `backstage.extraEnvVars` passthrough (deployment.yaml:234) and per-env secret wiring (Vault SecretProviderClass in prod, `-dev-secrets` k8s Secret in dev).
- Golden-path templates are registered as `type: url` GitLab locations in `app-config.local.yaml` (lines 78–91); production catalog locations come from the helm-mounted `app-config.production.yaml` (its `catalog.locations:` list is currently empty and populated via chart `backstage.appConfig.production`).

---

## Step 1 — CLI runner helper

**Create** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/runIntropyCli.ts`

A small injectable wrapper around `node:child_process.spawn` (no shell — args passed as array, so special chars in values are never shell-interpreted):

```ts
export interface RunIntropyCliOptions {
  command: string;          // binary path
  args: string[];
  cwd: string;
  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  logger: LoggerService;    // stream stdout->info, stderr->error, line-buffered
}
export interface RunIntropyCliResult { exitCode: number; stderrTail: string[] } // last ~50 stderr lines
export async function runIntropyCli(opts: RunIntropyCliOptions): Promise<RunIntropyCliResult>
```

Behavior:
- `spawn(command, args, { cwd, env, stdio: 'pipe' })`, `stdin: 'ignore'` (guarantees non-TTY so CLI prompts auto-disable, in addition to `--no-input`).
- Stream stdout to `logger.info`, stderr to `logger.error` (same as upstream `executeShellCommand`), while retaining the last 50 stderr lines in a ring buffer.
- Resolve with `{ exitCode, stderrTail }` for any exit code (caller maps codes); reject only on spawn `error` events. Translate `ENOENT` into a clear `Error("intropy CLI not found at '<path>'. Install it or set intropy.cli.path in app-config.")`.

## Step 2 — The action

**Create** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.ts`

Follow the exact pattern of `intropyWorkspaceTemplate.ts` (exported `examples` array + `createTemplateAction` with zod-callback schema).

```ts
export function createIntropyIntCreateAction(options: { config: RootConfigService }) {
  return createTemplateAction({
    id: 'intropy:int:create',
    description: 'Scaffolds an integration by running the intropy CLI (int create) against a blueprint.',
    examples: intropyIntCreateExamples,
    schema: {
      input: {
        blueprint: z => z.string().describe('Blueprint id, e.g. hello-world'),
        name: z => z.string().describe('Name of the integration to create'),
        targetPath: z => z.string().optional()
          .describe('Workspace-relative directory to generate into. Defaults to the workspace root.'),
        values: z => z.record(z.any()).optional()
          .describe('Blueprint parameter values (may be nested)'),
      },
      output: {
        outputDir: z => z.string().describe('Workspace-relative path of the generated integration'),
        blueprintVersion: z => z.string().describe('Resolved blueprint version'),
        blueprint: z => z.string(),
      },
    },
    async handler(ctx) { ... },
  });
}
```

Handler logic:

1. **Resolve output dir safely**: `const outDir = resolveSafeChildPath(ctx.workspacePath, ctx.input.targetPath ?? '.')` (same import as the existing action: `@backstage/backend-plugin-api`). `fs.ensureDir(outDir)`.
2. **Values file, not `--set`** (decision): `--set key=value` cannot express nested objects/arrays and forces string-flattening of special characters. Instead write the values map to a file and pass `-f`. Use `const tmpDir = await ctx.createTemporaryDirectory()` (built into `ActionContext`, auto-cleaned by the scaffolder — never lands in the published workspace) and write `values.yaml` there with `JSON.stringify(ctx.input.values, null, 2)` — JSON is a strict subset of YAML, so Go YAML parsers accept it and we need no new npm dependency. Skip the flag entirely when `values` is empty/undefined. (If the CLI's `-f` parser ever turns out to reject JSON, swap to the `yaml` package — one-line change.)
3. **Result file**: `const resultPath = path.join(tmpDir, 'result.json')` and pass `--output-json <resultPath>`. A file, not `-`, so CreateResult JSON can never interleave with progress output on stdout.
4. **Binary resolution** (see Step 3): `const cliPath = options.config.getOptionalString('intropy.cli.path') ?? 'intropy';`
5. **Invoke**:
   ```ts
   const args = ['int', 'create', blueprint,
     '--output', outDir, '--name', name,
     '--no-input', '--skip-install-skills',
     '--output-json', resultPath,
     ...(hasValues ? ['-f', valuesFile] : [])];
   const { exitCode, stderrTail } = await runIntropyCli({
     command: cliPath, args, cwd: ctx.workspacePath,
     env: { ...process.env },   // GITHUB_TOKEN, HOME, PATH pass through
     logger: ctx.logger,
   });
   ```
6. **Exit-code mapping**:
   - `2` → `throw new InputError(\`intropy rejected the input for blueprint '${blueprint}' (usage error). Check that all required blueprint parameters are provided in 'values'.\n${stderrTail.join('\n')}\`)` (`InputError` from `@backstage/errors`, already a transitive dep — add to backend `package.json` dependencies if not listed).
   - `1` (or anything else non-zero) → `throw new Error(\`intropy int create failed (exit ${exitCode}).\n${stderrTail.join('\n')}\`)`.
7. **Parse result + register outputs**:
   ```ts
   const result = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(resultPath, 'utf8')); // {blueprint, owner, repo, version, outputDir, values}
   ctx.output('outputDir', path.relative(ctx.workspacePath, result.outputDir)); // relative so downstream steps (fs, publish sourcePath) can use it
   ctx.output('blueprintVersion', result.version);
   ctx.output('blueprint', result.blueprint);
   ```
   Guard: if `result.outputDir` resolves outside `ctx.workspacePath` (`path.relative` starting with `..`), throw — belt-and-braces against the CLI writing elsewhere.
8. Log a one-line summary (`Created ${blueprint}@${version} at ${relOutputDir}`).

## Step 3 — Binary resolution + config

- **Config key**: `intropy.cli.path` (optional string; default `intropy` → resolved from `PATH`).
- **Modify** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/src/scaffolder/module.ts`:
  ```ts
  deps: {
    scaffolder: scaffolderActionsExtensionPoint,
    config: coreServices.rootConfig,        // from '@backstage/backend-plugin-api'
  },
  async init({ scaffolder, config }) {
    scaffolder.addActions(
      createIntropyWorkspaceTemplateAction(),
      createIntropyIntCreateAction({ config }),
    );
  },
  ```
- **Modify** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/app-config.local.yaml`: add
  ```yaml
  intropy:
    cli:
      path: ${INTROPY_CLI_PATH}   # optional; falls back to `intropy` on PATH
  ```
  (Backstage drops keys whose env substitution is unset, so this is safe.) Local devs on macOS install a darwin binary (`go install` / GoReleaser release download) — the container image binary is linux-only.
- Production image needs no config: `/usr/local/bin/intropy` is on PATH.

## Step 4 — Dockerfile

**Modify** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
# top of file, before first FROM
ARG INTROPY_CLI_VERSION=v0.3.0        # pin; bump deliberately
FROM ghcr.io/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli:${INTROPY_CLI_VERSION} AS intropy-cli
```

and in the final stage (after `FROM node:24-alpine`, near the mkdocs COPYs at lines 36–37):

```dockerfile
COPY --from=intropy-cli /usr/local/bin/intropy /usr/local/bin/intropy
```

Notes: using a named `FROM ... AS` stage (rather than `COPY --from=<image-ref>`) lets buildx pick the matching platform from the multi-arch manifest automatically for amd64/arm64 builds. Static binary from distroless runs fine on alpine; exec bit is preserved by COPY; readable by `USER node`. Pinning strategy: exact tag via `ARG` with a default, overridable with `--build-arg INTROPY_CLI_VERSION=...` from the CI pipeline (`templates/buildAndPublishImage.yml`) — later hardening can add a digest pin.

## Step 5 — Unit tests

**Create** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.test.ts`

**Modify** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/package.json`: add devDependency `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node-test-utils` (version from the Backstage 1.50.4 manifest; run `yarn add -D` then `yarn backstage-cli versions:bump --skip-migrate` is NOT needed — just install the release-matching version).

Test strategy (no real binary):
1. `jest.mock('./runIntropyCli')` — the action's process boundary is one mockable function.
2. Use `createMockActionContext({ input, workspacePath: mockDir })` from test-utils with `@backstage/backend-test-utils`' `createMockDirectory` (or `fs.mkdtemp` like the existing test does) for the workspace.
3. Cases:
   - **Happy path**: mock resolves `{exitCode: 0}` and, via `mockImplementation`, writes a fake CreateResult JSON to the `--output-json` path found in the received `args` — assert exact argv order (`['int','create','hello-world','--output',<abs>,'--name','demo','--no-input','--skip-install-skills','--output-json',<path>]`), assert `ctx.output` called with relative `outputDir` and `blueprintVersion`.
   - **Values file**: with nested `values`, assert `-f <file>` present and the file content parses back to the input map; assert no `-f` when values omitted.
   - **Exit 2** → rejects with `InputError` mentioning the blueprint and stderr tail; **exit 1** → plain `Error` with exit code.
   - **Path traversal**: `targetPath: '../../etc'` → `resolveSafeChildPath` throws.
   - **Binary path from config**: mock config with `intropy.cli.path: /opt/intropy` (use `mockServices.rootConfig({data: {intropy: {cli: {path: '/opt/intropy'}}}})` from `@backstage/backend-test-utils`) → runner called with that command.
4. Separate small test for `runIntropyCli` itself using a real fake executable: a `#!/bin/sh` script written to a temp dir (echoes to stdout/stderr, exits with requested code) — verifies streaming into a mock logger and stderr-tail capture without mocks.

# Implementation Plan: `intropy:int:create` Scaffolder Action + PoC Template

## Overview

Add a custom scaffolder action to the existing `scaffolder/intropy-actions` backend module that shells out to the `intropy` Go CLI (`int create`), get the static binary into the backend image via a multi-stage `COPY --from`, and ship one PoC template (hello-world blueprint) that generates code and opens a GitLab MR following the golden-record template's conventions.

Verified facts this plan relies on:
- `executeShellCommand` IS exported from the installed `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node@0.13.2`, but its implementation (checked `node_modules/@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node/dist/actions/executeShellCommand.cjs.js`) rejects with only `Command ${command} failed, exit code: ${code}` — no structured exit code, no stderr capture. Since we need exit-2-vs-1 mapping and a stderr tail in the error message, we write a ~40-line spawn wrapper modeled on it instead.
- `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node-test-utils` is NOT installed (checked node_modules) — the existing test file hand-tests helpers without an action harness. We add the test-utils package as a devDependency.
- Backstage 1.50.4; module registration at `packages/backend/src/index.ts:43`; helm chart at `charts/intropy-backstage` with `backstage.extraEnvVars` passthrough (deployment.yaml:234) and per-env secret wiring (Vault SecretProviderClass in prod, `-dev-secrets` k8s Secret in dev).

---

## Step 1 — CLI runner helper

**Create** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/runIntropyCli.ts`

A small injectable wrapper around `node:child_process.spawn` (no shell — args passed as array, so special chars in values are never shell-interpreted):

```ts
export interface RunIntropyCliOptions {
  command: string;          // binary path
  args: string[];
  cwd: string;
  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  logger: LoggerService;    // stream stdout->info, stderr->error, line-buffered
}
export interface RunIntropyCliResult { exitCode: number; stderrTail: string[] } // last ~50 stderr lines
export async function runIntropyCli(opts: RunIntropyCliOptions): Promise<RunIntropyCliResult>
```

Behavior:
- `spawn(command, args, { cwd, env, stdio: 'pipe' })`, `stdin: 'ignore'` (guarantees non-TTY so CLI prompts auto-disable, in addition to `--no-input`).
- Stream stdout to `logger.info`, stderr to `logger.error` (same as upstream `executeShellCommand`), while retaining the last 50 stderr lines in a ring buffer.
- Resolve with `{ exitCode, stderrTail }` for any exit code (caller maps codes); reject only on spawn `error` events. Translate `ENOENT` into a clear `Error("intropy CLI not found at '<path>'. Install it or set intropy.cli.path in app-config.")`.

## Step 2 — The action

**Create** `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage/packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.ts`

Follow the exact pattern of `intropyWorkspaceTemplate.ts` (exported `examples` array + `createTemplateAction` with zod-callback schema).

```ts
export function createIntropyIntCreateAction(options: { config: RootConfigService }) {
  return createTemplateAction({
    id: 'intropy:int:create',
    description: 'Scaffolds an integration by running the intropy CLI (int create) against a blueprint.',
    examples: intropyIntCreateExamples,
    schema: {
      input: {
        blueprint: z => z.string().describe('Blueprint id, e.g. hello-world'),
        name: z => z.string().describe('Name of the integration to create'),
        targetPath: z => z.string().optional()
          .describe('Workspace-relative directory to generate into. Defaults to the workspace root.'),
        values: z => z.record(z.any()).optional()
          .describe('Blueprint parameter values (may be nested)'),
      },
      output: {
        outputDir: z => z.string().describe('Workspace-relative path of the generated integration'),
        blueprintVersion: z => z.string().describe('Resolved blueprint version'),
        blueprint: z => z.string(),
      },
    },
    async handler(ctx) { ... },
  });
}
```

Handler logic:

1. **Resolve output dir safely**: `const outDir = resolveSafeChildPath(ctx.workspacePath, ctx.input.targetPath ?? '.')` (same import as the existing action: `@backstage/backend-plugin-api`). `fs.ensureDir(outDir)`.
2. **Values file, not `--set`** (decision): `--set key=value` cannot express nested objects/arrays and forces string-flattening of special characters. Instead write the values map to a file and pass `-f`. Use `const tmpDir = await ctx.createTemporaryDirectory()` (built into `ActionContext`, auto-cleaned by the scaffolder — never lands in the published workspace) and write `values.yaml` there with `JSON.stringify(ctx.input.values, null, 2)` — JSON is a strict subset of YAML, so Go YAML parsers accept it and we need no new npm dependency. Skip the flag entirely when `values` is empty/undefined. (If the CLI's `-f` parser ever turns out to reject JSON, swap to the `yaml` package — one-line change.)
3. **Result file**: `const resultPath = path.join(tmpDir, 'result.json')` and pass `--output-json <resultPath>`. A file, not `-`, so CreateResult JSON can never interleave with progress output on stdout.
4. **Binary resolution** (see Step 3): `const cliPath = options.config.getOptionalString('intropy.cli.path') ?? 'intropy';`
5. **Invoke**:
   ```ts
   const args = ['int', 'create', blueprint,
     '--output', outDir, '--name', name,
     '--no-input', '--skip-install-skills',
     '--output-json', resultPath,
     ...(hasValues ? ['-f', valuesFile] : [])];
   const { exitCode, stderrTail } = await runIntropyCli({
     command: cliPath, args, cwd: ctx.workspacePath,
     env: { ...process.env },   // GITHUB_TOKEN, HOME, PATH pass through
     logger: ctx.logger,
   });
   ```
6. **Exit-code mapping**:
   - `2` → `throw new InputError(\`intropy rejected the input for blueprint '${blueprint}' (usage error). Check that all required blueprint parameters are provided in 'values'.\n${stderrTail.join('\n')}\`)` (`InputError` from `@backstage/errors`, already a transitive dep — add to backend `package.json` dependencies if not listed).

7. **Parse result + register outputs**:
   ```ts
   const result = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(resultPath, 'utf8')); // {blueprint, owner, repo, version, outputDir, values}
   ctx.output('outputDir', path.relative(ctx.workspacePath, result.outputDir)); // relative so downstream steps (fs, publish sourcePath) can use it
   ctx.output('blueprintVersion', result.version);
   ctx.output('blueprint', result.blueprint);
   ```

# Backstage scaffolder backed by the intropy CLI

## Context

Today the Backstage golden-path templates (e.g. `docs/golden-path/templates/blueprints/golden-record/template.yaml`) re-implement blueprint rendering inside Backstage with a custom nunjucks action (`intropy:workspace:template`), duplicating what `intropy int create` already does. The CLI was just packaged into a Docker image (`ghcr.io/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`, distroless static binary) "for use in CI and Backstage", and it is scaffolder-ready: fully non-interactive (`--no-input`, prompts auto-disable off-TTY), stable exit codes (0/2 usage/1 runtime), and machine-readable results (`--output-json` → CreateResult `{blueprint, owner, repo, version, outputDir, values}`).

Goal: a new scaffolder action `intropy:int:create` that spawns the CLI inside the task workspace, so the CLI becomes the single scaffolding engine, plus one proof-of-concept template (hello-world blueprint) ending in a GitLab merge request. No changes to the Go CLI repo. Migrating the existing blueprint templates comes later, once proven.

Target app: `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage` (vanilla Backstage 1.50.x, new backend system). It already has a scaffolder backend module at `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/module.ts` — the new action follows that inline-action pattern.

## Key CLI facts (verified in intropy-cli repo)

- Invocation: `intropy int create <blueprint> --output <dir> --name <name> --no-input --skip-install-skills [-f values.json] --output-json <path>`
- Blueprints download at runtime from GitHub `integrio-intropy/intropy-blueprints` via api.github.com; auth via `GITHUB_TOKEN` env (needed if private, and to avoid the 60 req/h unauthenticated rate limit).
- `--skip-install-skills` hardcoded — avoids OCI pull from harbor.intropy.io (would need registry creds in the pod).
- `intropy int describe <blueprint> -o json` emits the Backstage-compatible parameter JSON Schema — use it to author the template's blueprint-parameters page.
- `-f` accepts YAML/JSON values files (JSON is a YAML subset), so nested values work without `--set` flattening.

## Implementation steps

All paths below are in `services/backstage/intropy-backstage` unless noted.

### 1. CLI runner helper — new `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/runIntropyCli.ts`

~40-line wrapper around `node:child_process.spawn` (args as array, no shell; `stdin: 'ignore'` guarantees non-TTY). Streams stdout→`logger.info`, stderr→`logger.error`, keeps a ~50-line stderr ring buffer. Resolves `{exitCode, stderrTail}`; rejects only on spawn errors, translating `ENOENT` into "intropy CLI not found at '<path>' — set intropy.cli.path". Modeled on `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node`'s `executeShellCommand`, which we can't use directly because it discards the exit code and stderr.

### 2. Action — new `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.ts`

Follow `intropyWorkspaceTemplate.ts`'s pattern (`createTemplateAction`, zod-callback schema, exported `examples`).

- **Input**: `blueprint` (string), `name` (string), `targetPath` (optional, workspace-relative), `values` (optional record).
- **Output**: `outputDir` (workspace-relative), `blueprintVersion`, `blueprint`.
- **Handler**:
  1. `resolveSafeChildPath(ctx.workspacePath, targetPath ?? '.')` (blocks traversal), `fs.ensureDir`.
  2. Write `values` as JSON to a file in `await ctx.createTemporaryDirectory()` (auto-cleaned, never published); pass via `-f`. Omit flag when no values.
  3. `--output-json <tmp>/result.json` (file, not stdout — avoids interleaving with logs).
  4. Binary: `options.config.getOptionalString('intropy.cli.path') ?? 'intropy'`; env: `{...process.env}` (passes GITHUB_TOKEN through).
  5. Exit-code mapping: 2 → `InputError` ("missing/invalid blueprint parameters" + stderr tail); other non-zero → `Error` with exit code + stderr tail.
  6. Parse CreateResult; guard that `outputDir` is inside the workspace; `ctx.output()` the relative outputDir, version, blueprint. Parse defensively (warn on missing fields) so CLI minor releases don't break runs.

### 3. Registration + config

- `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/module.ts`: add `config: coreServices.rootConfig` to deps; `scaffolder.addActions(createIntropyWorkspaceTemplateAction(), createIntropyIntCreateAction({ config }))`.
- `app-config.local.yaml`: add `intropy.cli.path: ${INTROPY_CLI_PATH}` (optional; local devs use a darwin binary on PATH — the image binary is linux-only).

### 4. Dockerfile — `packages/backend/Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
ARG INTROPY_CLI_VERSION=<current tag>          # top of file
FROM ghcr.io/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli:${INTROPY_CLI_VERSION} AS intropy-cli
...
# in final alpine stage:
COPY --from=intropy-cli /usr/local/bin/intropy /usr/local/bin/intropy
```

Named stage lets buildx pick the right platform from the multi-arch manifest; static binary runs on alpine. Pin exact version, override with `--build-arg` from CI.

### 5. Unit tests — new `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.test.ts`

Add devDependency `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node-test-utils` (release-matching version; not currently installed). `jest.mock('./runIntropyCli')` as the process boundary; `createMockActionContext` + temp workspace dir; `mockServices.rootConfig` for the binary-path case. Cases: happy path (exact argv, outputs registered from a fake result.json the mock writes), values-file round-trip / omitted when empty, exit 2 → InputError, exit 1 → Error, `targetPath: '../../etc'` throws, config-driven binary path. Separate small test for `runIntropyCli` using a real `#!/bin/sh` fake executable to verify streaming + stderr tail.

### 6. PoC template — new `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/docs/golden-path/templates/blueprints/hello-world-cli/template.yaml`

`metadata.name: hello-world-cli-blueprint`. Parameters: page 1 = name/description/owner (EntityPicker on Group); page 2 = blueprint params pasted from `intropy int describe hello-world -o json`. Steps:

1. `intropy:int:create` — blueprint `hello-world`, `targetPath: ./output/integrations/hello/${{ parameters.name }}`, values from parameters.
2. `roadiehq:utils:fs:write` (module already installed) — generate `catalog-info.yaml` (the CLI doesn't emit one), annotate `intropy.io/blueprint` + `intropy.io/blueprint-version: ${{ steps['create'].output.blueprintVersion }}`.
3. `publish:gitlab:merge-request` — follow the golden-record template's repoUrl/branch/sourcePath conventions.

Output links: MR URL + blueprint version.

Registration — dev: `type: file` location in `app-config.local.yaml` catalog locations (Template rule already allowed). Prod: `type: url` GitLab location added the same way the other golden-path templates are registered (via chart value `backstage.appConfig.production`).

### 7. GITHUB_TOKEN plumbing (helm chart `charts/intropy-backstage`)

Treat as required in prod (rate limits). Follow the existing `GITLAB_TOKEN` pattern in `templates/deployment.yaml`: dev → `secretKeyRef` key `github-token` in the `-dev-secrets` Secret; prod → add `github-token` to the Key Vault secrets list in `values-production.yaml`. Quick PoC alternative: `backstage.extraEnvVars` (already supported at deployment.yaml:234) with a manual secret — zero template changes.

## Verification

1. `yarn tsc && yarn test packages/backend` in the app repo.
2. Local: darwin `intropy` binary on PATH (or `INTROPY_CLI_PATH`), `GITLAB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.env`, `yarn start`; confirm `intropy:int:create` appears at `http://localhost:7007/api/scaffolder/v2/actions`.
3. Run the template from Create UI (or `POST /api/scaffolder/v2/tasks`); confirm CLI logs stream into the task log, MR is created, blueprint version shows in output.
4. Negative: omit a required blueprint value → InputError with exit-2 message; bogus `intropy.cli.path` → clear not-found error.
5. Image: `yarn build:all && yarn build-image`, then `docker run --rm --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/intropy <image> version`.

## Risks / gotchas

- Pod egress must allow `api.github.com` + `codeload.github.com` (tarball redirect).
- macOS dev needs a darwin binary; the image binary is linux-only.
- If the pod uses `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, the CLI may need a writable `$HOME/.cache` (emptyDir mount).
- Task workspace is disposed by the scaffolder after the run — no cleanup steps needed; values/result files live in the auto-cleaned temp dir.

app:
  # Should be the same as backend.baseUrl when using the `app-backend` plugin.
  baseUrl: http://localhost:3000

backend:
  # Note that the baseUrl should be the URL that the browser and other clients
  # should use when communicating with the backend, i.e. it needs to be
  # reachable not just from within the backend host, but from all of your
  # callers. When its value is "http://localhost:7007", it's strictly private
  # and can't be reached by others.
  baseUrl: http://localhost:7007
  # The listener can also be expressed as a single <host>:<port> string. In this case we bind to
  # all interfaces, the most permissive setting. The right value depends on your specific deployment.
  listen: ':7007'

# TechDocs configuration for development containers
techdocs:
  builder: 'local'
  generator:
    runIn: 'local' # Use 'local' in containers since Docker-in-Docker is complex
  publisher:
    type: 'local'

auth:
  # Use development environment for auth providers in local dev
  environment: development
  dangerouslyDisableDefaultAuthPolicy: true
  providers:
    # Guest auth allows running locally without any external auth provider
    guest: {}
    gitlab:
      development:
        clientId: ${GITLAB_CLIENT_ID}
        clientSecret: ${GITLAB_CLIENT_SECRET}
        audience: https://gitlab.com

permission:
  enabled: true
  policy:
    # Groups that can see all entities regardless of ownership
    adminGroupRefs:
      - group:default/guests
    # Entities owned by these groups are visible to all users
    sharedOwnerRefs:
      - group:default/dev-team

integrations:
  gitlab:
    - host: gitlab.com
      token: ${GITLAB_TOKEN}

# Catalog configuration for local development
catalog:
  # Disable providers that require external credentials (Microsoft Graph)
  providers:
    microsoftGraphOrg: null
  rules:
    - allow:
        [
          Component,
          System,
          API,
          Resource,
          Location,
          Template,
          User,
          Group,
          Domain,
        ]
  # File locations are relative to the backend process, typically `packages/backend`
  locations:
    - type: file
      target: ../../examples/entities-dev.yaml
    - type: file
      target: ../../examples/cluster.yaml
    - type: file
      target: ../../examples/org.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/blocks/extractor/template.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/blocks/file-transfer/template.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/blocks/loader/template.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/blocks/transactional/template.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/blueprints/golden-record/template.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/blueprints/point-to-point/template.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/docs/golden-path/-/blob/new-structure/templates/platform-defaults.yaml
    - type: url
      target: https://gitlab.com/integrio/intropy/customers/entrovia/gitops/-/blob/main/integration-endpoints/entrovia-sftp/catalog-info.yaml
    - type: url

apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: golden-record-blueprint
  title: Golden Record Blueprint
  description: Reconciles a shared entity (e.g. Customer, Product) from multiple source systems into a single authoritative record, with loaders to push the result to downstream targets
  annotations:
    backstage.io/techdocs-entity: component:intropy/golden-path-templates
    backstage.io/techdocs-entity-path: /blueprints/golden-record
    intropy.io/intrinsic-blocks: reconciler
  tags:
    - multi-source
    - reconciliation
    - master-data
    - blueprint
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: blueprint
    intropy.io/blueprint-type: golden-record
spec:
  owner: group:default/platform
  type: system
  dependsOn:
    - template:default/extractor-block
    - template:default/loader-block

  parameters:
    - title: System Details
      required:
        - systemName
        - entityName
        - description
        - domain
        - owner
      properties:
        systemName:
          title: System Name
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the system (lowercase, hyphens allowed)
          pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$"
          ui:help: "Example: customer-mdc"
        entityName:
          title: Entity Name
          type: string
          description: The entity type being reconciled (PascalCase, e.g., Customer, Product)
          pattern: "^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$"
          ui:help: "Example: Customer"
        description:
          title: Description
          type: string
          description: Brief description of the golden record system
          ui:widget: textarea
          ui:rows: 3
        domain:
          title: Domain
          type: string
          description: Business domain this system belongs to (select existing or enter new)
          ui:field: EntityPicker
          ui:options:
            allowArbitraryValues: true
            catalogFilter:

FROM node:24-alpine AS builder

ENV PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3
RUN apk upgrade --no-cache zlib && \
    apk add --no-cache python3 py3-pip g++ make && \
    pip3 install --break-system-packages mkdocs-techdocs-core==1.0.2

USER node
WORKDIR /app

COPY --chown=node:node .yarn ./.yarn
COPY --chown=node:node .yarnrc.yml backstage.json ./

ENV NODE_ENV=production

COPY --chown=node:node yarn.lock package.json packages/backend/dist/skeleton.tar.gz ./
RUN tar xzf skeleton.tar.gz && rm skeleton.tar.gz

ARG NPM_TOKEN
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/home/node/.cache/yarn,sharing=private,uid=1000,gid=1000 \
    if [ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]; then yarn config set 'npmScopes["integrio"].npmAuthToken' "$NPM_TOKEN"; fi && \
    yarn workspaces focus --all --production

# Remove unnecessary files from node_modules
RUN find node_modules \( -name "*.md" -o -name "*.map" -o -name "CHANGELOG*" \
      -o -name "LICENSE*" -o -name "*.ts" ! -name "*.d.ts" \) -type f -delete && \
      rm -rf node_modules/**/test node_modules/**/tests node_modules/**/__tests__

COPY --chown=node:node packages/backend/dist/bundle.tar.gz app-config*.yaml ./
RUN tar xzf bundle.tar.gz && rm bundle.tar.gz

# Final stage - no build tools
FROM node:24-alpine

RUN apk add --no-cache python3 && apk upgrade --no-cache zlib
COPY --from=builder /usr/lib/python3.*/site-packages/ /usr/lib/python3.12/site-packages/
COPY --from=builder /usr/bin/mkdocs /usr/bin/mkdocs

USER node
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NODE_OPTIONS="--no-node-snapshot"

COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app ./

CMD ["node", "packages/backend", "--config", "app-config.yaml", "--config", "app-config.production.yaml"]

apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cli-blueprint
  title: Hello World (intropy CLI)
  description: >-
    Proof-of-concept blueprint that scaffolds an integration by running the
    intropy CLI (int create) inside the scaffolder, instead of templating in
    Backstage. Ends in a GitLab merge request.
  tags:
    - blueprint
    - example
    - cli
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: blueprint
spec:
  owner: group:default/platform
  type: system

  parameters:
    - title: Integration Details
      required:
        - name
        - owner
      properties:
        name:
          title: Project Name
          type: string
          description: >-
            PascalCase identifier for the .NET project, namespace, and assembly.
            Dot-separated segments allowed (e.g. MyApi or Int1055.MyApi).
          pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$"
          ui:help: "Example: OrdersApi"
        description:
          title: Description
          type: string
          description: Brief description of the integration.
          ui:widget: textarea
          ui:rows: 3
        owner:
          title: Owner
          type: string
          description: Owning group (also selects the customer repository).
          ui:field: EntityPicker
          ui:options:
            catalogFilter:
              - kind: Group

    # The hello-world blueprint takes no parameters beyond `name` (supplied by
    # the CLI's --name). Blueprints with extra parameters would add a second
    # page here and pass them through the `values` input below. Author it from:
    #   intropy int describe <blueprint> -o json

  steps:
    - id: create
      name: Scaffold with intropy CLI
      action: intropy:int:create
      input:
        blueprint: hello-world
        name: ${{ parameters.name }}
        targetPath: "./output/integrations/${{ parameters.name | lower }}"
        # values:              # extra blueprint parameters go here (nested ok)
        #   someParam: ${{ parameters.someParam }}

    - id: catalog-info
      name: Generate catalog-info.yaml
      # The intropy CLI does not emit a catalog-info.yaml; write one here so the
      # created integration registers as a catalog Component.
      action: roadiehq:utils:fs:write
      input:
        path: "${{ steps['create'].output.outputDir }}/catalog-info.yaml"
        content: |
          apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
          kind: Component
          metadata:
            name: ${{ parameters.name | lower }}
            description: ${{ parameters.description }}
            annotations:
              intropy.io/blueprint: ${{ steps['create'].output.blueprint }}
              intropy.io/blueprint-version: ${{ steps['create'].output.blueprintVersion }}
          spec:
            type: service
            lifecycle: experimental
            owner: ${{ parameters.owner }}

    - id: create-merge-request
      name: Create Merge Request
      action: publish:gitlab:merge-request
      input:
        repoUrl: "gitlab.com?owner=integrio/intropy/customers/${{ parameters.owner | parseEntityRef({ defaultKind: 'group', defaultNamespace: 'default' }) | pick('name') }}&repo=integrations"
        title: "feat: Add ${{ parameters.name }} integration (intropy CLI)"
        description: |

kind: Template
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cli-blueprint
  title: Hello World (intropy CLI)
  description: >-
    Proof-of-concept blueprint that scaffolds an integration by running the
    intropy CLI (int create) inside the scaffolder, instead of templating in
    Backstage. Ends in a GitLab merge request.
  tags:
    - blueprint
    - example
    - cli
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: blueprint
spec:
  owner: group:default/platform
  type: system

  parameters:
    - title: Integration Details
      required:
        - name
        - owner
      properties:
        name:
          title: Project Name
          type: string
          description: >-
            PascalCase identifier for the .NET project, namespace, and assembly.
            Dot-separated segments allowed (e.g. MyApi or Int1055.MyApi).
          pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$"
          ui:help: "Example: OrdersApi"
        description:
          title: Description
          type: string
          description: Brief description of the integration.
          ui:widget: textarea
          ui:rows: 3
        owner:
          title: Owner
          type: string
          description: Owning group (also selects the customer repository).
          ui:field: EntityPicker
          ui:options:
            catalogFilter:
              - kind: Group

    # The hello-world blueprint takes no parameters beyond `name` (supplied by
    # the CLI's --name). Blueprints with extra parameters would add a second
    # page here and pass them through the `values` input below. Author it from:
    #   intropy int describe <blueprint> -o json

  steps:
    - id: create
      name: Scaffold with intropy CLI
      action: intropy:int:create
      input:

        # values:              # extra blueprint parameters go here (nested ok)

    - id: catalog-info
      name: Generate catalog-info.yaml
      # The intropy CLI does not emit a catalog-info.yaml; write one here so the
      # created integration registers as a catalog Component.
      action: roadiehq:utils:fs:write
      input:
        path: "${{ steps['create'].output.outputDir }}/catalog-info.yaml"
        content: |
          apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
          kind: Component
          metadata:
            name: ${{ parameters.name | lower }}
            description: ${{ parameters.description }}
            annotations:
              intropy.io/blueprint: ${{ steps['create'].output.blueprint }}
              intropy.io/blueprint-version: ${{ steps['create'].output.blueprintVersion }}
          spec:
            type: service
            lifecycle: experimental
            owner: ${{ parameters.owner }}

    links:

environment: production

# Workload Identity configuration (federated with AKS OIDC issuer)
workloadIdentity:
  clientId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Azure AD app registration client ID
  tenantId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Azure AD tenant ID

# Secret store provider configuration
vault:
  name: "your-vault-name"
  tenantId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Same as workloadIdentity.tenantId

  # Secrets to mount from Key Vault
  secrets:
    - objectName: backstage-azure-client-secret
      objectType: secret
      objectAlias: azure-client-secret
    - objectName: backstage-gitlab-token
      objectType: secret
      objectAlias: gitlab-token
    - objectName: backstage-harbor-username
      objectType: secret
      objectAlias: harbor-username
    - objectName: backstage-harbor-password
      objectType: secret
      objectAlias: harbor-password
    # Uncomment if PostgreSQL uses password authentication
    # - objectName: backstage-postgres-password
    #   objectType: secret
    #   objectAlias: postgres-password

backstage:
  baseUrl: "https://backstage.your-domain.com"

  database:
    # Use PostgreSQL for production (external Azure PostgreSQL)
    client: pg
    connection:
      host: your-postgres-host.postgres.database.azure.com
      port: 5432
      user: backstage@your-postgres-host
      # Password read from mounted Key Vault secret file
      password: "file:/mnt/secrets/postgres-password"
      database: backstage
      ssl:
        rejectUnauthorized: true

  azure:
    clientId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Your Azure AD app registration ID
    tenantId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Your Azure AD tenant ID
    clientSecret: ""  # Leave empty - will be read from Key Vault mount at /mnt/secrets/azure-client-secret

  # GitLab integration configuration
  gitlab:
    host: "gitlab.com"  # GitLab host (gitlab.com or your self-hosted instance)
    token: ""  # Leave empty - will be read from Key Vault mount at /mnt/secrets/gitlab-token

  # Harbor configuration
  harbor:
    baseUrl: "https://harbor.intropy.io"

content.text:
Done. Here's what I built to let Backstage scaffold via the `intropy` CLI.

## What was added

The approach: a custom scaffolder **action** `intropy:int:create` that runs the CLI inside the task workspace, so the CLI is the single scaffolding engine (no re-templating in Backstage), plus one PoC **template** that ends in a GitLab MR.

All changes live in two repos (nothing in `intropy-cli` — the CLI is only consumed):

**`services/backstage/intropy-backstage`**
- `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/runIntropyCli.ts` — a `spawn` wrapper (args as an array so no shell interpretation; `stdin` ignored so prompts stay off) that streams stdout/stderr into the task log, keeps a 50-line stderr tail, and translates `ENOENT` into a clear "not found — set intropy.cli.path" message.
- `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.ts` — the action. Writes `values` as JSON to `ctx.createTemporaryDirectory()` and passes `-f` (nested values survive, unlike `--set`), reads the CLI's `--output-json` result, maps **exit 2 → `InputError`** (bad params) and **other non-zero → `Error`** (both with the stderr tail), and registers `outputDir`/`blueprintVersion`/`blueprint` as step outputs. Binary path comes from config `intropy.cli.path`, defaulting to `intropy` on PATH.
- `scaffolder/module.ts` registers it alongside the existing action (added `coreServices.rootConfig` dep); `app-config.local.yaml` gets the `intropy.cli.path` key and registers the PoC template as a local `type: file` location.
- `packages/backend/Dockerfile` — a named `FROM ghcr.io/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli:v0.5.0` stage (buildx picks the right arch from the multi-arch manifest) and `COPY --from` of the static binary into the final alpine image.
- Helm chart: opt-in `backstage.github.enabled` flag injects `GITHUB_TOKEN` (for the CLI's blueprint download) from the dev/prod secret. Default off, so it's non-breaking.
- Two test files (15 tests) and `@backstage/backend-plugin-api` + `@backstage/errors` declared in backend deps.

**`docs/golden-path/templates/blueprints/hello-world-cli/template.yaml`** — the PoC. `hello-world` resolves to the `dapr-minimal-api` blueprint whose only parameter is `name`, so the form just collects name/description/owner; steps are `intropy:int:create` → write `catalog-info.yaml` (the CLI doesn't emit one) → `publish:gitlab:merge-request` following the golden-record repoUrl/branch conventions.

One deviation from the plan: rather than add `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node-test-utils` (not installed; would need a network/`NPM_TOKEN` install), I hand-rolled the action context in tests — matching how the existing `intropyWorkspaceTemplate.test.ts` already tests without a harness.

## Verified
- `yarn test packages/backend/src/scaffolder` — 15/15 pass; `yarn tsc` clean; lint clean on new files.
- `helm template`/`helm lint` — `GITHUB_TOKEN` absent when disabled, present (from `-dev-secrets`) when enabled.
- PoC template parses as valid YAML with the three expected steps.

**Not yet run** (needs your environment): the live end-to-end — starting the backend with a DB + GitLab/GitHub tokens and submitting a scaffolder task. To do that locally: put a darwin `intropy` binary on PATH (or set `INTROPY_CLI_PATH`), `yarn start`, confirm `intropy:int:create` at `/api/scaffolder/v2/actions`, then run the "Hello World (intropy CLI)" template.

This is a natural commit point — the two repos are independently committable (backend + chart in one, template in the other). Want me to stage and commit them, or would you prefer to run the live scaffolder task first?

# Backstage scaffolder backed by the intropy CLI

## Context

Today the Backstage golden-path templates (e.g. `docs/golden-path/templates/blueprints/golden-record/template.yaml`) re-implement blueprint rendering inside Backstage with a custom nunjucks action (`intropy:workspace:template`), duplicating what `intropy int create` already does. The CLI was just packaged into a Docker image (`ghcr.io/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`, distroless static binary) "for use in CI and Backstage", and it is scaffolder-ready: fully non-interactive (`--no-input`, prompts auto-disable off-TTY), stable exit codes (0/2 usage/1 runtime), and machine-readable results (`--output-json` → CreateResult `{blueprint, owner, repo, version, outputDir, values}`).

Goal: a new scaffolder action `intropy:int:create` that spawns the CLI inside the task workspace, so the CLI becomes the single scaffolding engine, plus one proof-of-concept template (hello-world blueprint) ending in a GitLab merge request. No changes to the Go CLI repo. Migrating the existing blueprint templates comes later, once proven.

Target app: `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/services/backstage/intropy-backstage` (vanilla Backstage 1.50.x, new backend system). It already has a scaffolder backend module at `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/module.ts` — the new action follows that inline-action pattern.

## Key CLI facts (verified in intropy-cli repo)

- Invocation: `intropy int create <blueprint> --output <dir> --name <name> --no-input --skip-install-skills [-f values.json] --output-json <path>`
- Blueprints download at runtime from GitHub `integrio-intropy/intropy-blueprints` via api.github.com; auth via `GITHUB_TOKEN` env (needed if private, and to avoid the 60 req/h unauthenticated rate limit).
- `--skip-install-skills` hardcoded — avoids OCI pull from harbor.intropy.io (would need registry creds in the pod).
- `intropy int describe <blueprint> -o json` emits the Backstage-compatible parameter JSON Schema — use it to author the template's blueprint-parameters page.
- `-f` accepts YAML/JSON values files (JSON is a YAML subset), so nested values work without `--set` flattening.

## Implementation steps

All paths below are in `services/backstage/intropy-backstage` unless noted.

### 1. CLI runner helper — new `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/runIntropyCli.ts`

~40-line wrapper around `node:child_process.spawn` (args as array, no shell; `stdin: 'ignore'` guarantees non-TTY). Streams stdout→`logger.info`, stderr→`logger.error`, keeps a ~50-line stderr ring buffer. Resolves `{exitCode, stderrTail}`; rejects only on spawn errors, translating `ENOENT` into "intropy CLI not found at '<path>' — set intropy.cli.path". Modeled on `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node`'s `executeShellCommand`, which we can't use directly because it discards the exit code and stderr.

### 2. Action — new `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.ts`

Follow `intropyWorkspaceTemplate.ts`'s pattern (`createTemplateAction`, zod-callback schema, exported `examples`).

- **Input**: `blueprint` (string), `name` (string), `targetPath` (optional, workspace-relative), `values` (optional record).
- **Output**: `outputDir` (workspace-relative), `blueprintVersion`, `blueprint`.
- **Handler**:
  1. `resolveSafeChildPath(ctx.workspacePath, targetPath ?? '.')` (blocks traversal), `fs.ensureDir`.
  2. Write `values` as JSON to a file in `await ctx.createTemporaryDirectory()` (auto-cleaned, never published); pass via `-f`. Omit flag when no values.
  3. `--output-json <tmp>/result.json` (file, not stdout — avoids interleaving with logs).
  4. Binary: `options.config.getOptionalString('intropy.cli.path') ?? 'intropy'`; env: `{...process.env}` (passes GITHUB_TOKEN through).
  5. Exit-code mapping: 2 → `InputError` ("missing/invalid blueprint parameters" + stderr tail); other non-zero → `Error` with exit code + stderr tail.
  6. Parse CreateResult; guard that `outputDir` is inside the workspace; `ctx.output()` the relative outputDir, version, blueprint. Parse defensively (warn on missing fields) so CLI minor releases don't break runs.

### 3. Registration + config

- `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/module.ts`: add `config: coreServices.rootConfig` to deps; `scaffolder.addActions(createIntropyWorkspaceTemplateAction(), createIntropyIntCreateAction({ config }))`.
- `app-config.local.yaml`: add `intropy.cli.path: ${INTROPY_CLI_PATH}` (optional; local devs use a darwin binary on PATH — the image binary is linux-only).

### 4. Dockerfile — `packages/backend/Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
ARG INTROPY_CLI_VERSION=<current tag>          # top of file
FROM ghcr.io/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli:${INTROPY_CLI_VERSION} AS intropy-cli
...
# in final alpine stage:
COPY --from=intropy-cli /usr/local/bin/intropy /usr/local/bin/intropy
```

Named stage lets buildx pick the right platform from the multi-arch manifest; static binary runs on alpine. Pin exact version, override with `--build-arg` from CI.

### 5. Unit tests — new `packages/backend/src/scaffolder/actions/intropyIntCreate.test.ts`

Add devDependency `@backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node-test-utils` (release-matching version; not currently installed). `jest.mock('./runIntropyCli')` as the process boundary; `createMockActionContext` + temp workspace dir; `mockServices.rootConfig` for the binary-path case. Cases: happy path (exact argv, outputs registered from a fake result.json the mock writes), values-file round-trip / omitted when empty, exit 2 → InputError, exit 1 → Error, `targetPath: '../../etc'` throws, config-driven binary path. Separate small test for `runIntropyCli` using a real `#!/bin/sh` fake executable to verify streaming + stderr tail.

### 6. PoC template — new `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/docs/golden-path/templates/blueprints/hello-world-cli/template.yaml`

`metadata.name: hello-world-cli-blueprint`. Parameters: page 1 = name/description/owner (EntityPicker on Group); page 2 = blueprint params pasted from `intropy int describe hello-world -o json`. Steps:

1. `intropy:int:create` — blueprint `hello-world`, `targetPath: ./output/integrations/hello/${{ parameters.name }}`, values from parameters.
2. `roadiehq:utils:fs:write` (module already installed) — generate `catalog-info.yaml` (the CLI doesn't emit one), annotate `intropy.io/blueprint` + `intropy.io/blueprint-version: ${{ steps['create'].output.blueprintVersion }}`.
3. `publish:gitlab:merge-request` — follow the golden-record template's repoUrl/branch/sourcePath conventions.

Output links: MR URL + blueprint version.

Registration — dev: `type: file` location in `app-config.local.yaml` catalog locations (Template rule already allowed). Prod: `type: url` GitLab location added the same way the other golden-path templates are registered (via chart value `backstage.appConfig.production`).

### 7. GITHUB_TOKEN plumbing (helm chart `charts/intropy-backstage`)

Treat as required in prod (rate limits). Follow the existing `GITLAB_TOKEN` pattern in `templates/deployment.yaml`: dev → `secretKeyRef` key `github-token` in the `-dev-secrets` Secret; prod → add `github-token` to the Key Vault secrets list in `values-production.yaml`. Quick PoC alternative: `backstage.extraEnvVars` (already supported at deployment.yaml:234) with a manual secret — zero template changes.

## Verification

1. `yarn tsc && yarn test packages/backend` in the app repo.
2. Local: darwin `intropy` binary on PATH (or `INTROPY_CLI_PATH`), `GITLAB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.env`, `yarn start`; confirm `intropy:int:create` appears at `http://localhost:7007/api/scaffolder/v2/actions`.
3. Run the template from Create UI (or `POST /api/scaffolder/v2/tasks`); confirm CLI logs stream into the task log, MR is created, blueprint version shows in output.
4. Negative: omit a required blueprint value → InputError with exit-2 message; bogus `intropy.cli.path` → clear not-found error.
5. Image: `yarn build:all && yarn build-image`, then `docker run --rm --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/intropy <image> version`.

## Risks / gotchas

- Pod egress must allow `api.github.com` + `codeload.github.com` (tarball redirect).
- macOS dev needs a darwin binary; the image binary is linux-only.
- If the pod uses `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, the CLI may need a writable `$HOME/.cache` (emptyDir mount).
- Task workspace is disposed by the scaffolder after the run — no cleanup steps needed; values/result files live in the auto-cleaned temp dir.

That line is **not from anything we built** — it's in the pre-existing `agent-skills` frontend plugin: `backstage-plugins/plugins/agent-skills/src/components/SkillDetailPage/index.tsx:30`. It's just picking a display title for a skill detail page, with a fallback chain.

Here's the whole "agentskills thing" and where each piece comes from:

**`io.agentskills.skill.name` is an OCI annotation key defined by the external Agent Skills spec** (agentskills.io) — not by Integrio. In that spec, an agent "skill" is packaged as an OCI artifact (`artifactType=application/vnd.agentskills.skill.v1`), and collections are OCI image indexes whose entries carry annotations like `io.agentskills.skill.name`, `io.agentskills.skill.ref`, and standard OpenContainers ones (`org.opencontainers.image.source/title/...`). You can see the key defined in several places in this workspace:
- CLI (the repo we're in): `internal/skillspec/media.go:10` and `internal/skill/oci/types.go:11` — `AnnotationSkillName = "io.agentskills.skill.name"`. The `intropy skills`/`skills collection` commands publish and read these artifacts.
- Backend plugin: `agent-skills-backend/src/router.ts:225` reads the annotation off the OCI manifest and returns it as `skillName`.

**The data flow for that snippet:**
1. The `intropy` CLI publishes skills to an OCI registry (harbor.intropy.io) with those annotations.
2. `@integrio/backstage-plugin-agent-skills-backend` fetches the manifest and exposes it via `api.getSkill(ref)` — returning a `SkillDetail` with both a parsed `config` (from the skill's own config blob) and the raw `annotations` map.
3. This frontend component builds the page title, preferring the skill's declared `config.name`, then falling back to the OCI annotation `io.agentskills.skill.name`, and finally the literal `'Skill'` if neither is present.

So the fallback exists because a skill *might* be published without a populated `config.name`, in which case the registry annotation is the next-best source for a human-readable name.
